title: A number converter
description:
Write a program that converts numbers between bases and to Roman numerals, one command per line:

```
bin 10
hex 255
oct 8
dec 0x1F
dec 0b1010
roman 1994
quit
```

prints

```
10 = 0b1010
255 = 0xff
8 = 0o10
0x1F = 31
0b1010 = 10
1994 = MCMXCIV
```

Commands (the command word ignores case; extra spaces are fine):

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `bin <n>`, `hex <n>`, `oct <n>` | `n` is a decimal `u64`; prints `<n> = 0b...`, `0x...` (lower case) or `0o...` |
| `dec <text>` | `text` is decimal, or has a `0b`, `0o` or `0x` prefix (prefix and hex digits in either case); prints `<text> = <decimal>` |
| `roman <n>` | `n` from 1 to 3999; prints the Roman numeral, or `Roman numerals go from 1 to 3999` |
| `quit` | Stops (so does the end of the input) |

Errors: a value that does not parse prints `Not a number: <value>`; a missing or extra value prints `Usage: <command> <value>`; an unknown command prints `Unknown command: <word>`. Blank lines are skipped.

**Do the conversions yourself** with loops and arithmetic: no `{:b}` / `{:x}` / `{:o}` formatting and no `from_str_radix`.
hints: To write a number in base `b`, take `n % b` as the last digit and divide `n` by `b`, until `n` is 0; then reverse the digits.

`text.strip_prefix("0x")` gives `Some(rest)` (the text after the prefix) or `None` when the text does not start with it: `if let Some(rest) = lower.strip_prefix("0x") { ... }`. The functions return an `Option`: `Some(value)` on success, `None` on failure, and `main` can `match` on it with `Some(n) => ...` and `None => ...`.

`match` against string literals needs a `&str`, not a `String`: after `let command_text = words[0].to_lowercase();`, borrow it with `let command: &str = &command_text;` and `match command { "bin" => ..., _ => ... }`.
`c.to_digit(16)` turns `'0'..='9'` and `'a'..='f'` into 0 to 15 (and gives `None` otherwise); `checked_mul` and `checked_add` with `?` turn overflow into `None`.
Roman numerals: walk a table from 1000 (`M`) down to 1 (`I`), including the subtractive pairs `CM`, `CD`, `XC`, `XL`, `IX` and `IV`, taking each value as many times as it fits.
requirements: Write one function per conversion: `to_base(n: u64, base: u64) -> String`, `parse_number(text: &str) -> Option<u64>`, `to_roman(n: u32) -> Option<String>`, and keep `main` to reading lines and printing results.
stretch: Add `fromroman <numeral>`, which turns a Roman numeral back into a number and rejects invalid ones like `IIII` or `VX`.
rules: Convert the digits yourself instead of using {:b}, {:x} or {:o}.
Parse the digits yourself instead of using from_str_radix.

examples.name: the example
examples.stdin:
bin 10
hex 255
oct 8
dec 0x1F
dec 0b1010
roman 1994
quit

examples.name: edge values
examples.stdin:
bin 0
hex 18446744073709551615
dec 0xffffffffffffffff
dec 0x10000000000000000
roman 3999
roman 4000
roman 0
dec 0O777
dec 0b102
dec 0x
examples.expected:
0 = 0b0
18446744073709551615 = 0xffffffffffffffff
0xffffffffffffffff = 18446744073709551615
Not a number: 0x10000000000000000
3999 = MMMCMXCIX
Roman numerals go from 1 to 3999
Roman numerals go from 1 to 3999
0O777 = 511
Not a number: 0b102
Not a number: 0x
